newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: KL big-cap shares lead market to strong finish.
newsitem.headline: KL big-cap shares lead market to strong finish.

text.p: Big-capitalised issues brought the market to a firm finish as local institutions bought actively, dealers and analysts said.
"There's buying out of Kuala Lumpur by local funds," said a Penang-based institutional dealer.
The key Composite Index of large-capitalised stocks rose 14.45 points or 1.34 percent to 1,096.33.
News and speculation drove a number of key stocks.
Public Bank local and foreign shares moved in drastically different directions on speculation over changes to its foreign shareholding limits.
The foreign tranche of Public Bank plunged 11.31 percent or 50 cents to 3.92 ringgit on the market's heaviest volume of 21.6 million.
Public's local stock jumped 7.23 percent or 24 cents to 3.56 on volume of 2.5 million.
Analysts cited a Public Bank circular which they say will allow foreign investors to buy into the local tranche of the stock, and not just limit themselves to the foreign shares.
"People whacked the foreign shares on the rumours. It's a bit confusing, but there are rumours the central bank has approved the plan," said a Jardine Fleming dealer.
